description: Somos Orbit-06, un grupo conformado por Keyra Wagner, Noel Suncar, Francisco Vásquez, I-Jen Lee, Julio Valdés y Nashla Alcántara. Nos gusta aprender, trabajar en equipo y compartir ideas. Estamos interesados en la tecnología, los sistemas, la innovación y la creación de soluciones.!!
summary: We developed Orbit SICES, a centralized scientific and educational web platform combining a microgravity combustion observatory with FlameZero, an open-ended, more than three-mission educational game. Using traceable open datasets from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Data Repository, the platform enables university professors, students, and researchers to visualize and compare key variables—such as initial and final oxygen, heat intensity, pressure, airflow, and flame displacement—across flagship NASA combustion investigations (including SAME, FLEX, BASS, Saffire, and ACME) and their sub-experiments, while clearly distinguishing real experimental data from educational simulations. Users can also connect their own AI API key to interpret scientific findings or integrate new datasets. To ensure inclusive STEM education, Orbit SICES offers bilingual navigation (English/Spanish), visual accessibility adjustments, and full guided-audio narration for users with disabilities. Understanding how fire behaves without gravity is essential for preventing, detecting, and extinguishing fires in spacecraft, space stations, and future Lunar and Martian habitats. Orbit SICES democratizes this critical space-safety research by transforming complex NASA data into accessible, interactive learning experiences.
details:
Orbit SICES is an easy-to-use web platform that brings together real NASA microgravity combustion experiments—such as BASS, BASS-II, Saffire, SAME, FLEX, and ACME—into a single observatory where users can read simple summaries and compare charts for variables like oxygen, heat intensity, pressure, airflow, and flame movement. It also includes an optional AI assistant where users can connect their own API key to interpret results or add new datasets, alongside FlameZero, an open educational game with more than three missions, virtual labs, characters, and interactive quizzes. By turning scattered, hard-to-read technical files into clear visuals and simple explanations, Orbit SICES saves time for university professors, students, and researchers, with the broader impact of democratizing space science and raising awareness about how to prevent, detect, and extinguish fires on spacecraft, space stations, and future habitats on the Moon and Mars. We built the platform using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Next.js, React, Node.js, Tailwind CSS, Recharts (for scientific data visualization), SQLite, Prisma ORM, Radix UI, the Canvas API (for the interactive web game), and Scratch (for the original development of the FlameZero game), managed with Git, GitHub, and Visual Studio Code and connected to open datasets from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. What makes our project creative is how it blends real scientific analysis, AI support, and gaming into one unified experience while maintaining strict scientific honesty—clearly separating real NASA experimental data from educational game animations so simulations are never presented as physical predictions. Finally, following mentor guidance, our team designed the platform around key human and educational factors: strict traceability to NASA sources, concise and accurate content tailored for university classrooms, bilingual support (English and Spanish), and universal accessibility through guided-audio narration, high-contrast modes, and reduced-motion options for users with disabilities.


Our team utilized Super Intelligence (SI) tools to accelerate software development, visual asset creation, technical text synthesis, and accessibility scripting, while the original project concept, scientific comparison structure, and educational game design were conceived entirely by our team:

  • Claude: Assisted with code debugging, refactoring, and structuring the data-comparison logic across experiments and sub-experiments.
  • Antigravity: Assisted with rapid full-stack prototyping, component layout generation, and development workflow acceleration.
  • Gemini: Assisted in synthesizing complex NASA PSI combustion investigation findings into concise, accurate summaries for university professors and students, as well as organizing technical documentation.
  • ChatGPT: Assisted in generating illustrative images for the educational experience and drafting guided-audio narration scripts and UI text.

All SI-generated images include visible watermarks indicating SI generation, and all SI-assisted code, text summaries, and audio scripts are explicitly acknowledged in our project's descriptive text and metadata.
